A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same COinCO research, and all supplied pages, tables, figures, and equations are readable. However, both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements. Referenced supplementary material covering training details, full prompts, and additional analyses is unavailable, limiting comparison of those aspects.

before.justification: V1 reports original human-validation results, semantic-prior analyses, context-classification experiments, objects-from-context prediction, and fake-localization evaluations.

after.justification: V2 reports original consensus-label validation and student-model experiments, alongside retained objects-from-context and fake-localization results.

M1.justification: Context annotation changes from Molmo labeling to unanimous agreement among Molmo-72B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and InternVL3.5-38B, with Qwen reasoning selected as primary annotations. Section 5.1 replaces VAE/BERT-based binary classifiers with three criterion-specific Qwen2.5-VL-3B students distilled from a 72B teacher. Objects-from-context prediction and the fake-score enhancement rule remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The COCO2017 domain, 80 object categories, and three principal applications remain. Context classification expands into separate size, location, and co-occurrence reasoning, with a dedicated unmanipulated-image evaluation. Original COCO images already participated in v1, so the expansion concerns task granularity and test scenarios rather than a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Table 3 replaces the VisualNet, SemanticNet, and VisSemanticNet comparison with comparisons between unfinetuned and distilled Qwen students. Section 4.2 adds comparative human assessment of three LVLMs, while v1's standalone Molmo object-presence benchmark is no longer reported. Comparator membership in Tables 2, 4, and 5 otherwise remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V1 balances context classification by supplementing generated images with original COCO images; v2 specifies a balanced 24,000-image consensus sample split into 20,000/2,000/2,000 training/validation/test images. Human context validation changes from 477 eligible cases to 1,000 consensus-selected images, comprising 300 in-context and 700 out-of-context cases. Evaluation adds criterion-level accuracy and a separate 2,000-original-image test; detector Table 2 replaces alignment rate and false-positive rate with F1.

E4.justification: V1's inpainting-success heatmap, clustering/GloVe analysis of semantic biases, and classifier input-modality comparison are no longer reported in the supplied v2. V2 adds analyses of criterion disagreements and reasoning preferences, plus an original-COCO evaluation intended to test dependence on inpainting artifacts. The oracle/practical fake-localization comparison remains.

E5.justification: V1 reports a Mann-Whitney U analysis with bootstrapped p = .002 and a Kruskal-Wallis test with p < .001 for semantic priors. These statistical tests are absent from the supplied v2. Neither supplied version reports repeated-run variability or confidence intervals for the principal task benchmarks.

E6.justification: V1's binary-classification results, including 76.90% VisSemanticNet accuracy, are replaced by criterion-level results averaging 73.7% on COinCO and 87.2% on original COCO after distillation. Human label agreement changes from 370/477 cases (77.57%) to 95.10% on a different 1,000-image consensus sample; these are not matched performance gains. Table 2 adds F1 results and drops alignment/false-positive rates. Tables 4–5 and Figure 6 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The objects-from-context category/clique formulation and clipped multiplicative fake-localization equation remain unchanged. Neither supplied PDF contains new or revised theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion replace the general visual-semantic context-classifier contribution with efficient, interpretable, criterion-specific reasoning through distillation, including applicability to real images. V1's abstract claim about discovering semantic priors in inpainting disappears. The core dataset, objects-from-context, and context-enhanced forensics contributions remain.

C2.justification: V1's interpretation that semantic features dominate visual features is replaced by arguments about successful reasoning transfer and genuine contextual understanding on original images. V2 adds explanations concerning rare-category annotation ambiguity, limitations of stronger inpainting generators, and contextual inconsistencies in real forgeries. The explicit limitation about inherently subjective context judgments disappears from the conclusion, although category restrictions and annotation disagreement remain acknowledged elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 identifies annotation and student checkpoints and their sizes, and newly specifies Molmo-7B for practical fake localization; v1's unspecified Molmo does not establish an actual model change there. It documents which consensus annotations are released and changes the code/data entry point from a GitHub repository to a project website. Detailed training instructions still depend on unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting knowledge distillation, newer LVLMs and generators, and contextual object recognition, including Distilling Step-by-Step, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3.5, and When Pigs Fly. BERT and MMDetection references disappear, and the YOLO citation changes to the original YOLO paper. The central positioning relative to COCO extensions and context-based forensics remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion, dataset rationale, validation sections, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Automated verification moves into Section 4.1, Section 5 is reframed around COinCO-enabled tasks, and task-specific protocols replace part of the earlier global description. Terminology changes from MLLM to LVLM, and author and acknowledgment text is updated.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the introductory image montage, and substantially redraws the pipeline diagram. Figure 3 loses the success-rate heatmap, Table 2 is transposed and reorganized, and Table 3 is replaced. Figures 4–7 retain their empirical content but are resized, reformatted, or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful consensus-label validation and criterion-level evaluations, but its higher human-agreement figure concerns a differently selected population. The new training protocol also claims 24,000 balanced images from a pool containing only 9,050 in-context images without explaining resampling or split independence. Together with the loss of the semantic-bias analysis and explicit subjectivity caveat, these unresolved tradeoffs prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
